artifact.cluster_ci95_note: 95% cluster-bootstrap intervals over source chunks (2000 resamples), informational

corpus.carve_bytes_source: sealed cache identity (sha256 of y and g); the cache carries no build metadata

bootstrap.rule: cluster bootstrap over the SCORED real-family chunks: np.random.default_rng(seed) draws n chunks with replacement per resample; every rung's accuracy on the resample is rounded to 4 decimals and the OLS slope against log2(plaintexts) refitted; one resample serves every rung and every role, so role differences are paired; the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles are the interval. The interval is over the scored chunks only: it says how far the slope moves if a different sample of held-out chunks of the same files is scored. It does not resample the fit side - which plaintexts fell into the lower rungs (one seed, one nesting) or where early stopping halted - and is not an interval on the slope of a re-drawn curve. The replicate rung is the run's only direct reading of that side, at the smallest rung, and it is informational.

cache_identity.X_note: restated from 0021's cache_identity verbatim (y, g, X hashes, shape, dtype); the feature array was first sealed and hashed there

protocol.caps_note: 0022's caps verbatim; selection_fit_seconds is dormant here (every fit is confirmatory) and memory_kill_gb is the live one

fit_corpus_described.convention: n_chunks in fit_corpus is the number of source chunks that CARRY ROWS, which is what the runner measures (1029); 1035 chunks were selected and 6 of them produced no row because every one of their 26 streams fell below the 4096-byte carve floor. The sealed extension corpus uses the same convention (n_chunks 2387 with rows, 2400 built).
fit_corpus_described.selection_rule: every whole 32768-byte chunk of each pinned blob that 0018's sealed selection (n_per_family 300, seed 20260909, recomputed here from tools/pivot/corpus_ext.py) does not use, in blob order, minus every chunk whose bytes hash to a sealed chunk's or to an earlier fit chunk's; no seed of its own

protocol.null_note: the null control permutes the whole fit block's labels with the split's own generator, exactly as 0021 and 0022 did at the same generator state, so the permuted label array is 0021's and its hash is sealed here; it is the first role in the order so that no other draw precedes it

reference_slopes_informational.builder_fixed_rows_is: 0021's builder_chunk_matched (0.1862, 1029 plaintexts) to builder_matched (0.201, 19413 plaintexts) at the same 26346 rows: the plaintext-only effect at a fixed row budget on the builder's content
reference_slopes_informational.builder_mixed_family_is: 0003's per-family curve for the builder's heterogeneous 'mixed' family (artifacts/pivot/per_family_curves.json: {'1000': 0.1059, '10000': 0.1135, '100000': 0.1154, '800000': 0.1143} over the four rungs, 0.002837 per decade): the record's closest in-distribution analogue of heterogeneous content, and it is flat
reference_slopes_informational.builder_mixture_is: 0003's headline slope 0.049121 per decade of manufactured FRAGMENTS over 2.9031 decades, converted; a different abscissa (0003's low rungs hold about one row per plaintext, this run's about 25.6)
reference_slopes_informational.builder_per_plaintext_is: 0021's builder_chunk_matched arm on the builder's evaluation set (0.1862 at 1029 builder plaintexts, artifacts/pivot/realfit_4096_rerun.json) to 0003's top rung (0.2395 at 40000 pool plaintexts, artifacts/pivot/deflate_curve.json): 5.2807 doublings of plaintexts with rows growing with them - the in-distribution per-plaintext rate on the builder's content
reference_slopes_informational.note: informational references for the prose and for one flag (the model's slope as a fraction of builder_per_plaintext_slope_per_doubling); none is a clause

protocol.reference_source: artifacts/pivot/realfit_4096_rerun.json ext_real_top1: real_model (M4), real_logistic (L3), floor_tree3 (D1), each fitted on this fit block in 0021's order and scored on this scoring set; 0022 reproduced all three with drift 0.0. The top rung IS that fit block row for row, so its three roles are the reproduction arms.

replicate_rung_1_hashes.rule: the smallest rung's rule and denominator under np.random.default_rng([seed, family_index + 1, 1]); informational: a direct reading of how much the smallest rung moves under a second draw of plaintexts

protocol.rung_rule: stratified_nested_by_family_chunk: per family, np.random.default_rng([seed, family_index + 1]) permutes its chunk ids with rows; rung d takes the first ceil(n_f / d); rows are the fit block's rows of those chunks in fit-block order

depth3_tree.why: 0003's depth3_tree verbatim (DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=3, random_state=0), gini, min_samples_leaf 1): 0.0969 banked

logistic.why: standardised inputs with C 1.0: the single most standard fix for an lbfgs logistic on 1108 unscaled hand-engineered columns

model.why: capacity plus regularisation plus a lower rate together: 800000 rows x 26 classes supports bigger trees than 63 leaves, and the deep-tree baseline gained 0.1459 -> 0.1812 from depth 8 to 16 at 4096

artifact.fit_record_top1_is: each record's top1 and top1_non_gutenberg are over the concatenated 260000 + 832 scoring set; per_family is over every family present in it - the builder's eight on the evaluation rows and the eight 'ext:'-prefixed extension families

partition.fit_order_rule: np.random.default_rng(20260825).permutation of the fit corpus's rows, so the recipes' last-10% validation split is a random tenth rather than one family (0021's fit block)

replicate_rung_1.rule: the smallest rung's rule and denominator under np.random.default_rng([seed, family_index + 1, 1]); informational: a direct reading of how much the smallest rung moves under a second draw of plaintexts

partition.row_identity_digest: blake2b-128 of the contiguous float32 feature row, over every scored row
partition.rung_rule: stratified_nested_by_family_chunk: per family, np.random.default_rng([seed, family_index + 1]) permutes its chunk ids with rows; rung d takes the first ceil(n_f / d); rows are the fit block's rows of those chunks in fit-block order

replicate_rung_1.note: informational: the smallest rung cut again under a second seeded nesting of each family's chunks and fitted with the same three recipes; the difference from rung 1 is a direct reading of the fit-side variance the scored-chunk bootstrap does not resample; never a verdict

rung.rule: the smallest rung's rule and denominator under np.random.default_rng([seed, family_index + 1, 1]); informational: a direct reading of how much the smallest rung moves under a second draw of plaintexts

slope_bootstrap.unit: accuracy on the real-family rows per doubling of plaintexts; cluster bootstrap over the scored real chunks
